expected.summary: Confirmed with its token and --dangerous, the job draws sheet 1 of design.json from the Demo parts: J1, C1, R1 and D1 on nets 5V and GND, and reads the nets back.

rows.reason: schematic create always wipes and redraws every sheet the design names; there is no call with nothing to draw.

expected.summary: The file given as --design is a parts file: a design needs a non-empty sheets list; refused at the preview.
The session has no such project open.
A Designer and a Layout are both running (the usual state once the board exists), and the call names neither --session nor --doc: E_AMBIGUOUS lists both instances with their documents.

An earlier schematic create job on this project was stopped by ending its worker process (Task Manager) while it ran, so its outcome is unknown and its operation keeps the sheets locked until operation resolve: E_CONFLICT target_locked, before any confirmation.
Run under a scope file that covers the project but does not allow dangerous operations (or does not cover the project): E_FORBIDDEN names what is missing; nothing is drawn.

While a schematic create job of this tool is still drawing in Designer, the session reports busy. Only --session is given: a busy Designer may not say which project it has open, and a --doc it cannot match would be E_NOT_FOUND.

A person leaves a modal dialog open in Designer before the call, such as Setup > Settings or Help > About. The session is reported blocked with the dialog's title; E_HUMAN_REQUIRED with action dismiss_dialog and a resume command. Only --session is given, since a blocked Designer may not say which project it has open.
The call returns the job (exit 0); Designer lost while the job draws ends it with change unknown, which job get reports as ok false with E_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, settled with operation resolve.

rows.unrunnable: The COM connection to Designer cannot be cut on demand at the moment of a call; driver tests D06 and D21 cover how the runtime handles a lost connection.

expected.summary: Designer holds unsaved changes from an earlier drawing; confirmed, the job draws over them as usual and saves nothing.

Confirmed, on the practice project's first drawing: the job's worker waits before its read-back, and meanwhile the 5V power symbol file the job wrote into the central library's SymbolLibs folder is deleted (--tamper). The read-back finds it missing, and the job ends with E_VERIFY_FAILED.
